title: "Hassabis: Use AI to Do More, Not Lay People Off"
description: "Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis argues companies should turn AI productivity gains into more work, not layoffs."
author: synesis
date: "2026-05-20"
image: cover.jpg
---

![Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind. Image from [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/demis-hassabis-ai-layoffs-deepmind-google-io/).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center"}

In a [WIRED interview](https://www.wired.com/story/demis-hassabis-ai-layoffs-deepmind-google-io/) ahead of Google I/O, [Demis Hassabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demis_Hassabis), CEO of Google DeepMind, pushed back on the idea that more capable AI coding models mean fewer engineers. Even while talking up Gemini 3.5 Flash's agentic coding (translating codebases, fixing deep bugs, writing operating systems from scratch), he said he had no idea why people predict doom for software developers, and suggested some of those predictions may have an ulterior motive like raising money.

His argument is that when engineers become three or four times more productive, the response should be to do three or four times more, not to cut headcount. He called companies that replace developers with AI short on imagination, and said Alphabet has a backlog of ideas, from drug discovery to game design, it would happily staff with the freed-up capacity. The interview ran alongside Google's I/O announcements, including the Antigravity coding tool and Gemini 3.5 Flash, as Google works to close the developer-adoption gap with Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex.
